_meta.description: Everything found during line-by-line verification that a human must review. An irregularity is raised whenever observed data contradicts the project brief, contradicts another official source, or cannot be traced to a primary source at all.

irregularities.title: The live contest contains no stocks, but the brief asks to invest in highly volatile stocks
irregularities.detail: The permitted instrument list for The Leap by AMP Futures (September 2026) contains 94 instruments, every one of them a futures contract. There are zero NASDAQ, NYSE or AMEX single-stock contracts. A stocks-only strategy cannot be executed in the currently live edition.
irregularities.observed: 94 futures / 0 equities. Exchange breakdown: CBOT 17, CBOT_MINI 15, CME 24, CME_MINI 18, COMEX 5, COMEX_MINI 6, NYMEX 7, NYMEX_MINI 2.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: A tradeable universe of highly volatile stocks.
irregularities.resolution: Either target a future stocks edition (the 'Magnificent Seven' stocks edition of March 2026 completed with a winning return of only +17.58% — see TV-CONTEST-MAG7-MAR2026), or translate the volatility research into the futures universe. This session built data/volatile_stocks.json as the evidence base for what extreme stock volatility actually delivers, and the futures master list for what the live contest actually allows.

irregularities.title: Captured stock-edition champions are lower than captured futures champions; cause is untested
irregularities.detail: In the captured completed-champion sample, the two stocks editions returned +29.90% (1.299x) and +17.58% (1.1758x), while the maximum futures champion is 53.2072x. This is an observed association only. Edition balance, leverage, caps, symbol set, duration, and participant behavior differ, so the sample does not prove that asset class caused the gap.
irregularities.observed: completed stocks: best 1.299x (n=2); completed futures: best 53.2072x (n=5); small champion-only sample.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Stocks deliver 5x-100x.
irregularities.resolution: Keep the stocks module as historical reference, use only live-eligible futures for this edition, and do not infer a causal strategy from champion summaries.

irregularities.title: No 100x contest-account outcome is attested by the captured official sample
irregularities.detail: The brief sets a 100x target. Across the 16 sourced contest records, including one in-progress row, the maximum captured return multiple is 53.2072x (+5,220.72%). Zero captured records are at or above 100x. This is a statement about the captured TradingView sample, not a universal upper bound.
irregularities.observed: >=5x: 2 cases. >=10x: 2 cases. >=20x: 1 case. >=50x: 1 case. >=100x: 0 cases.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Verified 100x returns available.
irregularities.resolution: Treat 100x as an unverified contest target. Never describe 53.2072x as a ceiling; it is only the maximum in the captured sample.

irregularities.title: The maximum-return objective is still constrained by account survival and margin
irregularities.detail: This is a virtual-money competition, so real-money risk management is not the objective. However, at 20:1 leverage on a $250,000 balance, $5,000,000 is the maximum initial notional. A loss equal to 5% of that fully deployed notional is $250,000. The account cannot be reset, and TradingView documents margin-call behavior in its simulator. Survival and margin feasibility are therefore optimization constraints, not investor-protection advice.
irregularities.observed: balance 250,000; leverage 20:1; maximum initial notional 5,000,000; account reset prohibited.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Maximize simulated returns; real-money risk management is not the objective.
irregularities.resolution: Evaluate drawdown and margin calls only as feasibility diagnostics. Do not turn the project into a real-money risk-management plan.

irregularities.title: Position limits change drastically between editions
irregularities.detail: NYMEX:CL1! was capped at 1.0 contract in the TradeStation July 2026 edition and 100.0 contracts in the AMP Futures September 2026 edition - a 100x change in capacity for the same instrument. CME:MBT1! moved 5.0 -> 25.0. Balance moved 100,000 -> 250,000 and leverage 10:1 -> 20:1.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Stable parameters.
irregularities.resolution: Re-read the live rules page before every edition. scripts/verify.py should be re-run against a freshly captured universe each time.

irregularities.title: Prize cut-off (300) is not visible on the public leaderboard (250 rows)
irregularities.detail: The rules award prizes to the first 300 participants, but the contest page exposes only the top 250. A participant in ranks 251–300 cannot verify the prize frontier from the public table, so a public rank-300 threshold must not be invented.
irregularities.observed: Latest captured page: top 250 out of 93,527 displayed participants; rules award no more than 300 prizes.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Observable prize boundary.
irregularities.resolution: Treat rank 250 as the last observable public row. Do not call it the actual rank-300 prize boundary and do not claim that crossing a live row guarantees a prize.

irregularities.title: Rules reference prize categories that the prize ladder does not define
irregularities.detail: The Prize Limitation clause reads 'In the event an Entrant qualifies for more than one (1) prize (i.e. the Top Trader Prize, MPT Prize or Flawless Run Prize)...', but the PRIZE DISTRIBUTIONS section for this edition defines only Top Trader Prizes. 'MPT Prize' and 'Flawless Run Prize' are undefined in this edition's rules, which suggests boilerplate carried over from another edition.
irregularities.observed: Two prize names referenced but not defined in this edition.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Internally consistent rules.
irregularities.resolution: Do not plan around MPT or Flawless Run prizes for this edition. Query TradingView support if these matter.

irregularities.title: The live edition's rules do not state a commission schedule
irregularities.detail: The TradeStation July 2026 rules state a $0.85 per-contract commission. The AMP Futures September 2026 rules were read in full and do not state a commission schedule. Absence of a rulebook line does not prove that every simulator or fill has zero cost.
irregularities.observed: No commission clause found in the September rules; $0.85/contract is edition-specific to the captured July rules.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Known transaction cost.
irregularities.resolution: Keep commission as not stated for the live rules. In Strategy Report sensitivity tests, declare zero and nonzero scenarios rather than silently assuming cost-free execution.

irregularities.title: Live participant counters differ across pages and capture times
irregularities.detail: TradingView landing and contest pages displayed slightly different participant counts when fetched at different moments. The live registration counter increased during the day. This is consistent with asynchronous snapshots rather than a fixed-data contradiction.
irregularities.observed: Latest captured pair (same session, 2026-09-17 ~20:56-20:58Z): contest page 96,236 versus landing page 96,230. Earlier same-day pairs: 96,095 vs 96,089; contest counts rose 93,527 -> 93,702 -> 95,709 -> 96,095 -> 96,236 across the five captures.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: n/a
irregularities.resolution: Every live count must carry a snapshot time or be described as displayed at capture; never combine counts from different fetches.

irregularities.title: The launch press release said 'pending regulatory review'; current CME and contest pages show XRP futures live
irregularities.detail: The 24 Apr 2025 press release announced a planned 19 May launch pending regulatory review. Current CME specification pages show the standard and micro XRP contracts, and the live TradingView rules list both as eligible. The old qualifier is historical and no longer an open master-list flag.
irregularities.observed: Current CME spec page shows a live front month and confirms the 50,000-XRP unit; both XRP contracts are in the September 2026 permitted universe.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Fully verified instruments.
irregularities.resolution: Resolved: both master-list rows are fully verified and the stale pending-launch flags have been removed.

irregularities.title: Partial locator scan initially misidentified SMCI's 2022 trough as the all-time low
irregularities.detail: A 2018-onward monthly locator scan suggested SMCI's October 2022 close (adjclose ~5.03 monthly low / 5.242 daily close on 2022-10-12) was the all-time trough. A full-history monthly scan (2007 IPO onward) disproved it: monthly lows ran ≈ 0.44–0.51 (adjusted) in the 2008–2009 financial crisis. No all-time multiple was ever published from the partial scan; the verified SMCI record (22.66x) is explicitly window-bounded to the fetched 2022 trough window and 2024 peak window.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: All-time extremes must come from all-time data.
irregularities.resolution: Corrected in research/evidence/VOLATILE-STOCKS-YAHOO-MONTHLY.md; data/volatile_stocks.json keeps only window-bounded claims and scripts/verify.py recomputes each multiple from archived endpoint values.

irregularities.title: Pine research cannot directly automate the competition Paper Trading account
irregularities.detail: Official TradingView documentation says Pine strategies simulate orders in the broker emulator and cannot place orders through the built-in Paper Trading account. Separately, the contest rules prohibit 60 or more order/position transactions per minute and warn that excessive activity, including various scripts, can trigger a ban. The user's no-manual-input instruction is satisfied for repository research; it must not be misrepresented as unattended competition execution.
irregularities.observed: Pine Strategy Report is hypothetical; direct built-in Paper Trading order placement is unsupported; contest transaction prohibition begins at 60 per minute.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Complete the research autonomously without asking the user for data entry.
irregularities.resolution: Generate and audit the research autonomously. Label the Pine code as a backtest/forward-test artifact only and make no claim of competition-account automation.

irregularities.detail: Between the original capture and the 2026-09-16 second pass, the Yahoo v8 chart API re-adjusted NVDA's historical adjclose: trough 2022-10-14 moved from 11.186728477478027 to 11.186724662780762 and peak 2024-06-18 from 135.20559692382812 to 135.20562744140625. Both generations recompute the same rounded multiple (12.09x). The archive in data/volatile_stocks.json was updated to the currently-served values. Vendor-tier data can drift between fetches; all other 7 symbols were bit-identical on re-fetch.
irregularities.observed: 6th-decimal adjclose change on 2 of 16 NVDA endpoint values; 0 changes on the other 14 endpoints.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Stable archived values.
irregularities.resolution: Rounded claims unaffected; archive now matches the live endpoint. No action beyond this record.

irregularities.title: TradingView Paper Trading help omits point value from its displayed short-futures formula
irregularities.detail: The official help page displays the long-futures formula with Quantity × Point Value. Its displayed short-futures formula omits Point Value, but the immediately following worked example multiplies by 10 contracts and a point value of 50 to obtain −$125. The formula and example are internally inconsistent.
irregularities.observed: Displayed short formula: (Average Fill Price − Ask price) × Quantity; worked example: (4520.25 − 4520.50) × 10 × 50 = −125 USD.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Unambiguous official P/L formula.
irregularities.resolution: Flag for manual review. The capacity model uses the contract multiplier symmetrically for directional point moves and does not quote the malformed short formula as complete.

irregularities.title: Market-data vendors block automated capture from datacenter IP ranges
irregularities.detail: Yahoo Finance returns HTTP 429 to every chart-API request made from the GitHub Actions runner range (both query1 and query2 hosts, confirmed by probe on 2026-09-17 with a browser User-Agent). Stooq returns a 795-byte JavaScript anti-bot challenge instead of CSV data. The capture pipeline therefore retries the identical vendor URLs through the public allorigins relay, a byte transport. Every relayed payload is validated against the expected vendor symbol and OHLC invariants and spot-verified against independent in-session captures; the transport used is recorded per symbol in data/market_history_index.json.
irregularities.observed: 20/20 symbols HTTP 429 direct from runner; stooq cl.f..eth.f all returned the identical 795-byte JS challenge; allorigins relay returned the full 27,505-byte CL=F 1-year JSON with valid chart structure.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Automated, reproducible ingestion of daily futures history from a free vendor.
irregularities.resolution: Open. The relay works but is a third-party dependency; a licensed feed (e.g. CME settlement-based continuous series) or a residential-IP capture remains the clean fix. Workflow probe annotations document the failure mode.

irregularities.title: Several selected micro/crypto futures have only one day of vendor history
irregularities.detail: SOL=F, MSL=F, XRP=F and MXP=F each expose at most one daily bar (validRanges limited to ['1d','5d']), so the selected CME:SOL1!, CME:MSL1!, CME:XRP1! and CME:MXP1! cannot be backtested or volatility-ranked from vendor data yet, despite being eligible competition instruments with rules caps.
irregularities.observed: Vendor listing gaps: CME:SOL1!, CME:MSL1!, COMEX:SIC1!, CME:MBT1!, CME:MET1!, NYMEX:MNG1!, NYMEX:MCL1! and CME:XRP1! returned exactly 1 daily bar for the 2-year window (newly listed on the vendor), so they cannot be backtested; 8 of 20 selected symbols are excluded from the simulation for insufficient history.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Testable history for every selected instrument.
irregularities.resolution: Open. These tickers will accumulate history over time; re-run the capture pipeline in later sessions. Their capacity arithmetic (rules cap x multiplier x price) is already verified from official sources and does not depend on vendor history.

irregularities.title: Yahoo front-month close differs from the TradingView continuous quote by 3.32% for crude oil
irregularities.detail: For 2026-09-16, the captured Yahoo CL=F series closed at 105.83 while the TradingView CL1! overview page displayed 102.43. The Yahoo front contract is 'Crude Oil Oct 26' while the TradingView continuous series and the intraday capture time (16:49-17:23 GMT-4) differ. All other cross-checked symbols landed within 2%. The verifier warns above 2% and hard-fails above 15% to catch genuine ticker mix-ups.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Vendor and platform prices for the same underlying should be close enough to confirm the ticker mapping.
irregularities.resolution: Open, informational. Documented caveat for cross-source price comparisons; not treated as a mapping error.

irregularities.title: Leaderboard frontier partially static across two captures while the mid-board moved
irregularities.detail: Between captures 1 and 2 (~3 hours, US after-hours) rank 1 and rank 250 were byte-identical while the mid-board moved (rank 50 +$28,139.75, rank 100 +$11,027.50). Capture 3 (2026-09-17T16:56:00Z, ~19.5 hours after capture 1, spanning one US trading day) moved ALL FOUR frontiers up: rank 1 +$31,400.00 (same holder), rank 50 +$75,661.00 vs capture 2, rank 100 +$28,661.85, rank 250 +$31,380.50, with new holders at 50/100/250. The quiet 3-hour window does not generalize; the frontier is a rising moving target (H18).
irregularities.observed: data/frontier_history.json captures 1-3; the value captured at rank 50 on 2026-09-17T00:30:00Z (RIA-JANGHU +$1,172,236.00) had slid to rank 69 by 16:56 and the value at rank 100 (msm223034 +$971,231.00) had slid to rank 114.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Understanding how the prize frontier moves over time.
irregularities.resolution: Refined, still open. Continue capturing the frontier through the end of the contest (2026-09-30T12:00:00Z); the practical planning fact is that the P/L required to hold any public rank is rising, and the last visible rank (250) underestimates the cash prize frontier (H19).

On the fourth pass (index fetched_at 2026-09-17T03:15:40Z, workflow run 35177491162) BTC=F succeeded with 504 sessions (2024-09-17 -> 2026-09-17) and XRP=F/MXP=F succeeded with a single session each: the vendor only lists recent history for those tickers (no firstTradeDate in the meta), so their single session is a data-availability limit, not a relay failure. irregularities.title: Newly listed COMEX:SIC1! vendor close differs from the TradingView snapshot quote by 2.09%
irregularities.detail: The 2026-09-17 vendor capture for SIC=F (single session, first valid close) differs from the TradingView continuous-quote snapshot value by 2.09%, above the 2% warning threshold. SIC1! is newly listed on the vendor, the snapshot quote is from 2026-09-16 17:21 GMT-4, and the front-contract month and capture time differ between the two sources. This is the same cross-source price-comparison caveat as IR-19 (crude oil, 3.32%) and is a documented limitation of comparing a single-session vendor close against a continuous-futures quote, not evidence of a bad mapping. scripts/verify.py warns at >2% and fails at >15% (mapping-error bound).
irregularities.observed: verify warning 'market_history.quote_delta: COMEX:SIC1!' (2.09%); data/market_history_index.json record for COMEX:SIC1! (1 session) vs data/live_contest_snapshot.json quote row.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: Line-by-line verified inputs; anything unexplained is flagged.
irregularities.resolution: Open, informational. Will tighten automatically once SIC=F accumulates multi-session history and the quote snapshot is refreshed in a later session.

irregularities.title: Displayed rank-50 frontier decreased between two same-day captures; the board is corrected, not append-only
irregularities.detail: Between 2026-09-17T16:56:00Z and 2026-09-17T19:04:00Z the displayed rank-50 realized P/L fell from +$1,247,897.00 to +$1,244,313.50 (-$3,583.50), and the exact row value previously at rank 50 (trader rajgaurav009, same percentage and dollars) appeared at rank 49. Realized P/L on closed positions cannot shrink for a still-registered account, so the net effect is exactly one fewer row ahead of it; the most parsimonious explanation is one removal from the public board among rows ranked 1-48 at capture 3 (disqualification or correction). Official rules sections 05, 09 and 16 reserve at-any-time disqualification rights; the official pages publish no board-change log, so removals are only observable indirectly, as here. Capture 5 (20:58Z) then showed the same rank-49/rank-50 rows byte-identical again and the rank-100 boundary pushed down by one new row, i.e. after the single correction the high board was stable for at least 1.9 hours; the frequency of such corrections cannot be measured from the public page.
irregularities.observed: Capture 3 -> capture 4: rank 1 unchanged at +$2,335,125.00; rank 50 -$3,583.50 with the previous row intact one place higher at rank 49; rank 100 +$12,309.65; rank 250 +$2,235.50; participants 95,709 -> 96,095. Capture 4 -> capture 5: rank 1 and rank 50 unchanged to the cent; rank 100 +$2,747.50 with the previous rank-100 row at rank 101; rank 250 +$3,454.50; participants 96,095 -> 96,236.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: A leaderboard frontier is a ratchet: it can only rise as the contest progresses.
irregularities.resolution: Treat every captured frontier as a point-in-time display, never as a guaranteed floor or final threshold. The verifier enforces profit ordering only within a capture, never across captures. Hypothesis H20 records the observation and its test.

irregularities.title: Leaderboard percentage and dollar columns do not always reconcile to the cent within a row
irregularities.detail: The public board displays realized P/L as a two-decimal percentage and as dollars. Re-deriving dollars as 250,000 x percentage / 100 does not always reproduce the displayed dollars: at capture 5, rank 50 displays 497.73% and $1,244,313.50 (re-derived $1,244,325.00, a $11.50 difference) and rank 250 displays 264.30% and $660,759.50 (re-derived $660,750.00, a $9.50 difference), while rank 1 and rank 100 reconcile exactly. The differences are inside the +/- $12.50 bound implied by rounding a longer internal P/L to two percentage decimals, so this is a display-rounding artifact, not a contradiction between sources. It is recorded because the verifier allows the bound rather than exact equality, and a reader comparing the two columns will notice the mismatch.
irregularities.observed: Capture 5 (2026-09-17T20:58:00Z): rank 50 -$11.50 and rank 250 -$9.50 versus the percentage-implied dollars; ranks 1 and 100 exact. Every capture from 1 to 5 stays inside the +/- $12.50 bound.
irregularities.expected_by_brief: The dollar and percentage columns of one row should reconcile exactly.
irregularities.resolution: scripts/verify.py enforces the +/- $12.50 rounding bound on every capture row and never tolerates a larger gap; all displayed values are quoted verbatim in the evidence files and no value is smoothed.
